prompt: Write the body (about 180 words) of a demand letter from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer before a lawsuit. Accident: low-speed head-on collision. Injury: neck strain. Use the exact placeholders [CLIENT_NAME], [LOSS_DATE] and [DEMAND_AMOUNT]. No other names or dates. (Internal reference C-1188; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing on behalf of our client, [CLIENT_NAME], regarding the collision that occurred on [LOSS_DATE]. Our client was traveling in their lane when the other vehicle crossed the center line and struck head-on at low speed. The impact was not minor in its effect: our client was thrown forward and back against the seat, and was left with a neck strain that has required ongoing treatment, including physical therapy and restricted range of motion that has interfered with daily work and sleep.

The liability picture is straightforward. Your insured left the proper lane without warning, and the responding officer's report documents the position of both vehicles at rest. There is no reasonable basis on which to attribute fault to our client.

Our client has provided all treatment records and billing statements requested to date. The medical documentation links the complaints directly to the collision, and the treating providers have noted no prior history of similar symptoms.

On behalf of our client, we demand payment of [DEMAND_AMOUNT] to resolve all claims arising from this loss. This demand will remain open for thirty days from the date of this letter. If we do not receive a substantive response within that period, we will file suit without further notice and seek all damages available under law.
